newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus Emirates deal boosts A330-200 programme.
newsitem.headline: Airbus Emirates deal boosts A330-200 programme.

text.p: Airbus Industrie's $2 billion deal to supply 16 jets to Emirates airline will have little impact on the European consortium's position in the international aircraft market, but puts its A330-200 programme on solid footing.
State-owned carrier Emirates and Airbus signed the deal for the 16 new A330-200 aircraft, with an option for seven more, on Monday in Dubai.

The order by 11-year-old Emirates is the first by a Middle East airline and brings to 56 the number of firm orders for the widebody twin jet since the November 1995 launch of the A330-200 programme, Airbus said.

International Leasing Finance Corp (ILFC) ordered 38 A330-200s in March and Korean Airlines ordered two in May, an Airbus spokesman said. ILFC has options for eight more jets and Korean has options for 10 more.
The Airbus spokesman said the most important thing about the deal was that it firmly established the new A330-200 programme.
"It's a nice deal which helps get the A330-200 programme off the ground quickly," spokesman Alain Dupiech said.
Although sizeable, the deal does not break new ground for Airbus since the A330-200s will replace 16 older Airbus aircraft being sold by Emirates.
"Every time there's a new deal announced, people try to find out if there's something special or new about it," Dupiech said. "That's not the case. This is a normal, straightforward deal."
The deal also appears to do little to alter the fight for global market share between Airbus and U.S. giant Boeing Co.
Industry sources said Airbus still trails Boeing with about 41 percent of the market compared to the U.S. manufacturer's 50 to 55 percent.
Airbus does not publish profit figures, but its sales in 1995 reached $9.6 billion, a mark Airbus passed in June, one of the sources said.
Airbus managing director Jean Pierson said in Dubai on Monday that Airbus had agreed to assist Emirates with the sale of the 16 A310 and A300-600s which the airline it is replacing.
The industry sources said the assistance would probably amount to no more than informing Emirates of any clients who might be interested in its used planes.
Airbus beat off competition from Boeing's 767 plane and said engines to power the jets would be made by either Rolls Royce Plc or General Electric Co.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace -- part of Daimler- Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
